rule: The eye level is a straight horizontal line; objects above it are seen from below and objects below it are seen from above.
A set of parallel lines receding from the viewer converges to one vanishing point on the eye level; lines parallel to the picture plane do not converge.
Keep the two vanishing points far apart; closely spaced vanishing points produce warped perspective in which square forms look distorted.
Do not include too wide a field of view; forms toward the edge of a wide view become misshapen and distorted.
A circle in perspective is an ellipse whose long axis is always at right angles to the axis of the cylinder or disc, whatever its tilt.
In normal two-point perspective vertical lines are drawn vertical, with no vanishing point.
Shade on a curved surface is darkest along the edge nearest the light, because reflected light brightens the rest of the shade side.
Darken the parts of an object that face away from the light source.
Cast shadows follow perspective: parallel edges cast parallel shadows that converge to the same vanishing points.
Draw an irregular object by first fitting it inside a box drawn in correct perspective.
The intersection of a rectangle's diagonals locates its true perspective centre.
